THE ROLE

We’re looking for a high-performing strategic finance professional to join our growing Product Finance team. Training is one of Baseten's fastest-evolving businesses and it won't be the last new product line we launch. You'll own the economics of Training end to end and be the finance owner for new products as they go from idea to launch to scale, partnering directly with Product, Engineering, Infrastructure, and GTM leadership on the pricing, margin, and capacity decisions that shape each business. This is a builder role: much of what you'll own doesn't exist yet as a model, a dashboard, or a process.

This role is ideal for someone with 5 to 8 years of experience across strategic finance, investing, and/or investment banking who wants broad exposure to company-building inside a fast-scaling AI infrastructure company. Experience at a usage-based company is a plus.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Build and maintain cost-to-serve models for Training engagements across compute, delivery time, and reserved capacity

 - Own Training pricing and recommend structures across committed engagements, usage-based pricing, and packaged offerings

 - Track training capacity utilization and tie capacity plans to pipeline

 - Run the monthly Training business review across bookings, utilization, margin, pipeline, and renewal and expansion trends

 - Own the Training forecast and annual plan, including compute needs, unit costs, and multi-year P&L

 - Partner with Product on new products from concept onward, building pre-launch business cases, cost-to-serve views, and go/no-go recommendations

 - Set launch pricing and packaging for new products

 - Define success metrics and scale criteria at launch




REQUIREMENTS

 - Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Finance, or Economics

 - 5+ years of experience in strategic finance at a high-growth company, PE/VC investing, and/or investment banking

 - Excellent financial modeling and analytical skills, including building unit economics or cost-to-serve models from raw usage and cost data

 - Ability to synthesize complex information into clear recommendations for executives

 - Comfortable building from scratch and making decisions with incomplete data in a fast-moving environment

 - Strong attention to detail with a bias toward ownership and execution

 - Excellent communication and presentation skills

 - High intellectual curiosity and interest in AI / infrastructure / developer tooling

 - Advanced Excel / Google Sheets skills; familiarity with SQL or BI tools is a plus




NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with GPU compute economics or cloud infrastructure

 - Familiarity with how ML model training and fine-tuning work

 - Experience with product-led growth economics, such as free tiers, credits, and conversion

 - Experience pricing or launching a new product line



BENEFITS

 - Competitive compensation, including meaningful equity

 - (U.S. only) 100% coverage of medical, dental, and vision insurance for employee and dependents

 - Flexible PTO policy including company wide Winter Break (our offices are closed from Christmas Eve to New Year's Day!)

 - Paid parental leave

 - Fertility and family-building stipend through Carrot

 - (U.S. only) Company-facilitated 401(k)

 - Proven experience directly managing engineers in a cloud infrastructure, platform engineering, or SRE context (not managing managers).

 - Extensive hands-on experience with Kubernetes, with the ability to engage credibly in architectural discussions and code reviews.

 - Demonstrated ability to drive projects end-to-end — from specification to execution — and coach your team to do the same.

 - Track record of recruiting and growing engineering talent.

 - Openness to learning about ML infrastructure; prior machine learning experience is not required.

Networking and compute are no longer separate disciplines; they are converging. The massive throughput of H100, B200, and NVL72 architectures enables and demands a new approach where communication is co-optimized alongside computation. We are entering an era where the network is an active accelerator, leveraging smart hardware offloads and direct interconnects to ensure that data movement operates at wire-speed.

In this role, you will go beyond network configuration to architect the software fabric that unifies thousands of GPUs into a cohesive operating system. While you will leverage the best of the open-source ecosystem, you won't be limited by it. Where off-the-shelf solutions stop, you will build from scratch, engineering the primitives required to co-optimize communication and compute for Disaggregated Serving, Wide Expert Parallelism (WideEP), and lightening cold starts.



RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Make RDMA First-Class: You will work on integrating RDMA/RoCE/InfiniBand capabilities directly into our inference stack, helping us move beyond TCP/IP to unlock order-of-magnitude improvements in bandwidth and latency.

 - Optimize Distributed Inference: You will implement and tune the networking layers necessary for efficient Disaggregated KV Cache Offload and WideEP, ensuring seamless communication across NVLink and InfiniBand for our MoE models.

 - Enable Serverless-Grade Startup Speeds for LLMs: You will work deeply with checkpointing and storage mechanisms to enable sub-10-second startup for trillion-parameter models.

 - Deep-Dive into Hardware: You will characterize and validate networking performance on bleeding-edge clusters (H100/H200, B200/B300, GB200/300 NVL72), writing the acceptance tests that ensure our hardware delivers peak achievable throughput and minimal latency.

 - Build Observability: You will design the tools that let us visualize packet flow, congestion, and effective bandwidth across the GPU interconnects, helping us diagnose complex distributed system behaviors.

 - Optimize Kernels: You will work with communication libraries (NCCL, NVSHMEM) and potentially write custom communication kernels to overlap compute and data transfer.

THE ROLE

Container runtimes were designed for general-purpose software workloads. AI inference is not a general-purpose workload.

Running large models at production scale exposes cracks in every layer of the container stack: runtimes unaware of GPU memory constraints, images that take minutes to pull when a model needs to scale to thousands of replicas, and isolation mechanisms that weren’t designed for the multi-tenant serving environments that production AI requires. The tools the industry has relied on for a decade weren’t built for this, and patching around those limitations at higher layers only goes so far.

Baseten owns the entire pipeline, from the moment a developer pushes a model to the moment a request gets a response. That vertical ownership means we can fix these problems at the root. The Runtime Fabric team is doing exactly that: purpose-building the container runtime and storage layers for AI inference workloads, led by some of the world’s top containerd maintainers.

As Engineering Manager for Storage Products on the Runtime Fabric team, you will lead the engineers who build and run the storage products behind that stack: the Baseten Delivery Network (BDN), which sits in the cold start path of every model on the platform, the snapshotters and filesystems that expose model weights and container images to a running container, and the storage that model deployment and training need next. The team is advancing the next generation of caching for inference workloads, from the origin tier to the GPU host. You will own reliability for the area as a measured outcome, report to the head of Runtime Fabric, and stay close to the code through design and code review. If you’ve managed systems engineers and have hands-on experience with caching, content-addressable storage, or distributed filesystems, we’d love to talk.

EXAMPLE INITIATIVES

 - How the Baseten Delivery Network (BDN) makes cold starts fast https://www.baseten.co/blog/how-the-baseten-delivery-network-bdn-makes-cold-starts-fast/

 - Extending BDN from model weights to container image layers, training checkpoints, and deployment artifacts

 - Lazy-loading snapshotters and block-level delivery (EROFS, FUSE, ublk) so a container can start before the full image or model has arrived

RESPONSIBILITIES

Team Leadership and Culture

 - Hire and grow a team of 5 to 10 systems engineers with storage, caching, and Linux expertise

 - Run the team’s planning and delivery: scope work against the Runtime Fabric roadmap, set priorities, and ship on a predictable cadence

 - Provide regular coaching, feedback, and career development support to your direct reports

 - Own on-call health for the team’s services, including escalation paths and follow-through on incidents

Technical Direction

 - Guide the architecture and evolution of the Baseten Delivery Network: the tiered caching and weight delivery product that makes cold starts 2-3x faster and eliminates thundering herd failures during burst scaling events

 - Shape storage products tailored to Baseten’s workloads: extend BDN from model weights to container images, training checkpoints, and deployment artifacts, and define the interfaces that model deployment, training, and customers use to reach them

 - Oversee the on-host side of delivery: lazy-loading snapshotters, EROFS and overlayfs layouts, and block-level delivery (FUSE, ublk) for multi-gigabyte files

 - Own reliability of the delivery path as a measured outcome: end-to-end instrumentation from snapshotter initialization to first inference request, targets for cold start and cache behavior, tolerance for failing upstream registries and object stores, and safe rollout of changes to a path every customer depends on

 - Make the delivery path work across heterogeneous clusters and cloud providers, each with its own object store and network

 - Review designs and code across the area, and take on hands-on work where it unblocks the team

 - Champion the team’s contributions back to containerd and the snapshotter ecosystem alongside the maintainers on the Runtime Fabric team

Cross-Functional Partnership

 - Act as the point of contact for storage across Baseten, ensuring model deployment, training, and platform teams have the integration support they need

 - Optimize requirements for the underlying storage platforms with the infrastructure team: object storage, local NVMe and block storage, and network bandwidth per cluster, so that capacity and provider decisions account for what the delivery path needs

 - Manage the team’s dependencies in both directions: sequence work that model deployment, training, and infrastructure teams block on, and negotiate interfaces and timelines with the teams and upstream projects the storage path depends on

 - Work with the head of Runtime Fabric and product stakeholders to prioritize storage investments based on customer impact and infrastructure reliability

 - Communicate team progress, technical trade-offs, and incidents clearly to the team and to leadership

REQUIREMENTS

 - Experience managing a team of engineers in a systems, infrastructure, or storage context, including hiring and performance management 

 - Hands-on background in distributed storage systems, content-addressable storage, or large-scale caching infrastructure

 - Strong systems programming background in Go, Rust, and/or C/C++, with the ability to engage credibly in code reviews and architectural discussions

 - Working knowledge of the Linux storage stack: filesystems, the page cache, block devices, and mounts

 - Understanding of how container images are structured, stored, and delivered at scale

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence without authority across teams

NICE TO HAVE

 - Contributions to containerd/containerd, snapshotter projects (stargz, soci, nydus, overlaybd), distribution/distribution, or closely related open-source projects

 - Familiarity with lazy-loading snapshotters or peer-to-peer image distribution

 - Experience with EROFS, FUSE, ublk, or io_uring

 - Experience building or operating CDN, object storage, or large-scale caching infrastructure

 - Experience running storage services on Kubernetes

Every agent on Baseten Sandboxes runs in its own microVM. Agents call models, reach tools and APIs, expose services, and more and more often talk to each other. Networking built into today's cloud providers was not designed for very large numbers of isolated machines that suspend, resume, and exchange data constantly.

The Agent Infra team builds its own networking stack for sandboxes, designed from the start for that scale. It runs in user space, with VPP (FD.io http://FD.io) as its main data plane technology, and is built from virtualized network functions (VNF/NFV): carrier-grade, low-latency packet processing designed for very large numbers of agents. In September 2026, Baseten acquired Blaxel https://www.baseten.co/blog/blaxel-is-joining-baseten-to-build-the-future-of-agentic-cloud/, whose sandboxes, storage, and networking are the foundation for Baseten Sandboxes https://docs.baseten.co/sandboxes.

You'll build multi-tenant virtual private networking that connects each customer's agents and services privately and securely, using modern overlay technologies.

We are building a cloud, not just using one. We want engineers who expose the network as a programmable API and write the code, not operators who push router and switch configuration. The team is small and ownership is big: we ship in weeks and months, not multi-year programs.

This role is separate from Baseten's GPU-to-GPU networking. Here you'll own how sandboxes connect to each other, to Baseten services, to customer networks, and to the internet.

If you've built user-space data planes, virtualized network functions, or multi-tenant cloud networking and want to design one for agents, we'd love to talk.



EXAMPLE INITIATIVES

 - Blaxel is joining Baseten to build the future of agentic infrastructure https://www.baseten.co/blog/blaxel-is-joining-baseten-to-build-the-future-of-agentic-cloud/

 - Expose the network as a programmable API that the rest of the platform calls

 - Cut latency and raise connection scale for agent-to-agent and agent-to-service traffic

 - Build routing that sends each request to the nearest region and keeps connections working as sandboxes suspend and resume

 - Build secure ingress and egress for sandboxes, including firewalling, static egress IPs, and custom domains with managed TLS

 - Build L7 proxies for request inspection, filtering, secret injection, and auditing

 - Own per-sandbox addressing, including IPv6, and network isolation between tenants

 - Build observability for the packet path across guest, host, and network, and debug production issues end to end

 - Work closely with the compute, storage, GPU infrastructure, and datacenter teams



REQUIREMENTS

 - Experience with user-space packet processing (DPDK, VPP, or similar) or virtualized network functions (VNF/NFV)

 - Experience building multi-tenant networking in production (VXLAN, GENEVE, VRF)

 - Experience building a software-defined network, overlay network, or packet-processing data plane in production

 - You write production code: strong systems programming in Rust, Go, and/or C/C++. Network architects are welcome if they build, not only configure

 - Solid grounding in TCP/IP and routing

 - You move fast and like owning a problem end to end on a small team

Storage decides how fast agent sandboxes start and how safely they share data. Agents need a filesystem that thousands of sandboxes mount at the same time, with strict isolation and the consistency agents need. Agent context is mostly small files, so the access patterns look very different from storage built for large files.

The Agent Infra team builds Agent Drive, the distributed filesystem that agent sandboxes mount over FUSE, and the storage underneath it. The work uses tiered caching, replication, content-addressed data, and Linux filesystem internals. In September 2026, Baseten acquired Blaxel https://www.baseten.co/blog/blaxel-is-joining-baseten-to-build-the-future-of-agentic-cloud/, whose sandboxes and Agent Drive filesystem are the foundation for Baseten Sandboxes https://docs.baseten.co/sandboxes.

We are building a cloud, not just using one, so storage is designed for many tenants from day one. The team is small and ownership is big: we ship in weeks and months, not multi-year programs.

If you care about page cache coherency, FUSE, replication protocols, and content-addressable storage, we'd love to talk.
